exercise.name: Half Squat Side Reach

reference.title: Half Squat Side Reach (male)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time because the proxy blocked it, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip, knee and ankle, with trunk rotation)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you sit down and reach, exhale as you stand and bring the hands back.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s down, short hold, about 1 s up per side

prescription.tempo: Controlled, about 1 s down, 1 s up
prescription.frequency: 2-3 times a week or as a warm-up
prescription.progression: Deeper squat, longer hold, then hold a light medicine ball or dumbbell in both hands

cues.text: Feet a little wider than the hips, toes slightly out, hands together in front of the chest.
Sit back into a half squat and reach both hands out to the right at shoulder height; the chest turns with them.
Knees over the toes, heels down, hips stay square to the front; eyes on the hands.
Stand up and bring the hands back to the chest.
Repeat the reach to the left.

mistakes.mistake: Knees collapsing inward as you turn
mistakes.fix: Keep both knees over the 2nd-3rd toe; turn the chest, not the knees.
Sit the hips back and keep the weight over the mid-foot.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to reach farther
mistakes.fix: Reach only as far as you can with a long spine.
Keep the pelvis facing forward; the rotation comes from the upper back.

kinematics.norm: A little wider than the hips (clinical opinion)
Half squat: about 60-90 degrees of knee flexion (clinical opinion); depth is driven mostly by knee range of motion (Zawadka 2020)
Moderate forward lean with an upper-back rotation toward the reach (clinical opinion); more lean moves demand from knee to hip (Straub 2024)
Hands out to the side at about shoulder height (reference movement; clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s each way (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 15140, Half Squat Side Reach, video (movement reference)
Zawadka et al. 2020, How are squat timing and kinematics in the sagittal plane related to squat depth? (J Sports Sci Med 19:500-507)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Back discomfort: turn less and keep the hands closer to the body.
regressions: Bodyweight squat with the arms forward.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Main knee extensors: control the half squat and drive the stand. Knee range of motion was the strongest contributor to squat depth (Zawadka 2020).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Main knee extensors: control the half squat and drive the stand. Knee range of motion was the strongest contributor to squat depth (Zawadka 2020).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extensor for the stand; a more forward trunk shifts demand from the knee to the hip (Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extensor for the stand; a more forward trunk shifts demand from the knee to the hip (Straub 2024).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Help extend the hips and keep the knees tracking (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Help extend the hips and keep the knees tracking (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hip extensors with the glutes; little change in length at the knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hip extensors with the glutes; little change in length at the knee (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Turn the chest toward the reach and back (clinical opinion); the obliques on the reaching side and the opposite side work together.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Turn the chest toward the reach and back (clinical opinion); the obliques on the reaching side and the opposite side work together.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the arms out at shoulder height (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the arms out at shoulder height (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs over the pelvis while the trunk turns (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the knees over the toes as the weight shifts toward the reach (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the knees over the toes as the weight shifts toward the reach (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a long spine in the forward lean (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a long spine in the forward lean (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps hold the arms out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps hold the arms out (clinical opinion).
